name: Chicken sausages, peppers, and kabocha with ajvar
time: 45 minutes, most of it in the oven
intro: Sausages roasted on one pan with squash and sweet peppers until everything browns in their fat — served the Balkan way, with a pile of ajvar on the side and bread to drag through it.
needs: ½ large kabocha (about 1½ lbs), in 1-inch wedges
2 red bell peppers, in thick strips
Sourdough or rice: a thick slice, or 1 cup cooked, per serving

steps.text: Heat the oven. If the kabocha is too hard to cut, put it in whole for 10 minutes first.
Toss the squash with half the olive oil and a pinch of salt, spread it on a sheet pan, and give it 10 minutes on its own.
Toss the peppers with the rest of the oil and salt and add them to the pan with the sausages, leaving room between everything.
Roast, turning the sausages once, until they're browned and the squash edges are dark. Raw chicken sausage is done at 165°F; precooked just needs to brown.
Toast the sourdough in a skillet with a little oil while the pan finishes.
Everything on the plate, a big spoonful of ajvar beside it, lemon squeezed over the vegetables.

how_it_works: Sausage brings its own fat, and on a hot sheet pan that fat runs out and roasts the vegetables around it — the pan seasons itself. Ajvar is what's served with grilled sausages across the Balkans: smoky, sweet, a little sharp, exactly what cuts the richness.
swaps: Any sausage works — pork or chicken.
Sweet potato instead of kabocha, same timing.
No ajvar made yet? Lemon, olive oil, and a pinch of chile flakes over the top.
leftovers: Pack a lunch before you sit down: sliced sausage, squash, and peppers over 1 cup of rice, ajvar on the side.
